newsitem.title: SWITZERLAND: Swiss Re plans to spin off ART unit.
newsitem.headline: Swiss Re plans to spin off ART unit.

text.p: Swiss Reinsurance Co, the world's second largest reinsurance company, confirmed a newspaper report that it plans to spin off its Alternative Risk Transfer (ART) actitivies into a separate legal unit.
"We are thinking along those lines," spokesman Otto Kern told Reuters in response in an inquiry. The company would issue a statement on April 28.
Switzerland's Sonntags Zeitung reported on Sunday the new unit would be named Swiss Re New Markets and would initially be 100-percent owned by Swiss Re.
Sonntags Zeitung speculated that Credit Suisse Group could later take a stake in Swiss Re's new company, but Kern would not confirm this.

Credit Suisse Group and Swiss Re have been cooperating in the area of ART -- which combines derivative financial instruments with insurance and risk management -- since 1995 and the two companies have formed three joint ventures in this area.
The new company has also been evaluating the possibility of creating an exchange for the trading of derivative-based insurance products in Zurich, the paper added.
Walter Kielholz, chief executive of Swiss Re, set up Swiss Re's ART division in 1995 as part of Swiss Re's strategy to expand its activities in ART and life reinsurance.
One of the challenges the new company would focus on would be to tackle the problem of insurance for catastrophes, a subject insurance and reinsurance companies are trying to solve.
Insurers worry there is not enough capital available in traditional insurance companies markets to cover large natural catastrophes, such as earthquakes.
One way to cover such risks is to securitise the risks by creating a marketable instrument, which then can be sold to a much larger group of investors.
So far the only derivatives on catastrophes are traded on the Chicago Board of Trade (CBOT).
